content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Aiken

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree and documented project management education—no work experience necessary. This makes the credential accessible to career-changers and early-career professionals entering Aiken's nuclear energy, advanced manufacturing, and healthcare sectors. Verify your education history and you're ready to proceed.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot-camp course. Delivered entirely online, this intensive format fits working professionals' schedules while covering PMI's full curriculum. You'll engage with active certified practitioners and complete all required contact hours in a concentrated timeframe.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, apply directly to PMI with proof of your education hours and secondary degree. Pay the associated exam fee and await PMI's verification. This step formally registers you as a CAPM candidate and clears you to sit for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor support—to reinforce key concepts. Schedule your proctored exam through PMI's testing partner. The computer-based test assesses your grasp of project management fundamentals and professional responsibility.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn professional development units (PDUs) over a three-year renewal cycle to keep your CAPM active. Pursue training, volunteer roles, or professional activities aligned with PMI's continuing-education standards. Renewal demonstrates your commitment to staying current in project management practice.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: Is the CAPM a good starting credential for {city} professionals?
fq_items.answer: Yes. The CAPM is one of the most recognized entry-level PM credentials and is highly regarded across industries in {city_state}. It demonstrates PM knowledge to employers even before you have years of experience.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.

fq_items.question: Is this training delivered online?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Our CAPM training is fully live-virtual — no travel required. {city} students attend via video conference from wherever they are.
